text: hey everybody one of the ways that many Christians today negotiate with the biblical text in order to structure power and values in favor of their
identity politics and their boundary maintenance is by either denying that women held positions of ecclesiastical Authority within early Christianity and
within the Hebrew Bible or insisting that they only did so because there weren't any worthy men around and so
they had to step up and assume a position that usually they are not qualified to hold now there are no data
that actually support the latter interpretation and the former interpretation is a renegotiation because we have plenty of texts in the
Bible that identify women who held positions of authority within early Christianity we have archaeological data that indicate women were holding such
positions up until the fourth or fifth or maybe even the sixth Century CE as well and that renegotiation usually
involves reinterpreting or ignoring the passages that refer to women holding such position such as women who are
referred to as deaconesses they reinterpret this as a reference to women who are just serving understanding that word for Deaconess as just a generic
reference to service we also have the re-reading of Romans 16 7 which according to the earliest Christians is
a pretty clear reference to a woman named yunya as an apostle we have folks like John chrysostom and theodorant and origen praising the
outstanding character of this woman who was an apostle and about a thousand years after Romans was written we begin
to see manuscripts that accentuate the name in a way that indicate it's the name of a man and so it would be many
centuries after Paul wrote Romans that's this re-reading of yunya as a man's name
began to creep in and these days folks will argue either that this is a reference to a man or that it is a
reference to a woman named Union but it doesn't identify her as an apostle it just says she's well known to the apostles and these readings don't really
have much data to support them and conflict with the earliest readings that we find among the early Christian Community if you'd like more discussion
on yunya as the first woman Apostle I would highly recommend yunya the first woman Apostle by Elden J app and this
was published in 2000 five if you would like a great discussion on the subjugation of Women Within historical
Christianity I would highly recommend Beth Allison Barr's book The Making of biblical Womanhood how the subjugation
of women became gospel truth
